title: Corpus

description.main: Daisuke Yokota's first book of nude photographs, published by Artbeat Publishers, Tokyo, in 2014 in an edition of 1,000 copies. Seventy-two pages of black-and-white images of bodies tangled in a closed room, re-photographed and chemically degraded in Yokota's usual manner; edited by Shigeo Goto, designed by Tetsuro Furutani.
description.extended:
Corpus is the Japanese photographer Daisuke Yokota's first book of nude photographs, published by Artbeat Publishers in Tokyo in 2014 in an edition of 1,000 copies.

The 72-page softcover, about 35 by 26 cm, prints more than forty black-and-white images full page. Bodies lie tangled together in a closed room, and the pictures were made the way Yokota makes most of his work: he re-photographs his own prints and processes the film at high temperature, so grain, scratches and chemical residue settle over the figures. The book was edited by Shigeo Goto, whose G/P Gallery runs the Artbeat imprint, and designed by Tetsuro Furutani. It appeared in the year Yokota's first European solo exhibition closed at Foam in Amsterdam, a year after he received the first Outset Unseen award.

Yokota (b. 1983, Saitama) published a run of self-published and small-press books in the early 2010s, from Back Yard and Site/Cloud, also from Artbeat, to Vertigo and Toransupearento. Corpus turns the same abrasive process on the human figure rather than on landscape, and it precedes the more domestic nudes of Taratine, published by Session Press the following year.
description.artist_bio: Daisuke Yokota (b. 1983, Saitama) is a Japanese photographer known for re-photographing and chemically degrading his own prints. He received the first Outset Unseen award in 2013, had his first European solo exhibition at Foam, Amsterdam, in 2014, and won the Foam Paul Huf Award in 2016. His books include Back Yard, Site/Cloud, Vertigo, Toransupearento, Taratine and Matter / Burn Out.
